title: Retained compact-support Hom transposes and canonical tensor and composition maps
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: an algebraic closure $k$ of a finite field of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, a positive integer $m$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$. For a finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, not necessarily separated, write $D_T=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, using the derived pullback and tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\mathrm{CTF}_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ be the full finite-Tor constructible domain [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; let $\mathrm{BC}_T$ denote the bounded constructible domain. An edge $e:X\to Y$ consists of a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f$, a retained compactification $c_f=(j_f,p_f)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and a nonnegative integer upper bound for the topological Krull dimension of its ambient scheme [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Define $S_e=Lf^*$, $F_e=Rp_{f,*}j_{f,!}$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and $G_e=\nu_X^*H_eR\nu_{Y,*}$, where $H_e$ is the ordinary-etale right adjoint at $c_f$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Put $W_e=G_e\Lambda_Y$. These are the existing fixed-coefficient constructions, at the retained compactification, with no ambient pro-etale adjunction assumed.

For a bounded-below object $B\in D_Y$ and a bounded-below etale-origin object $M\in D_X$ with a retained witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], let $\mathrm{hom}_e:\operatorname{Hom}(F_eM,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_eB)$ be the specified transported ordinary-etale Hom bijection: conjugate by the witness, use compact-support site comparison, the comparison adjunction, the ordinary-etale adjunction, and fully faithful comparison pullback; this is the specified Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] on the bounded-below comparison class. Define $\varepsilon_{e,B}=\mathrm{hom}_e^{-1}(1_{G_eB})$. The canonical etale antecedent of $G_eB$ is $H_eR\nu_{Y,*}B$; its comparison is the identity in these coordinates. The coefficient unit has finite Tor interval $[0,0]$, and pullback followed by tensor preserves the finite-Tor constructible input domain. These supply the domain certificates used below.

Write $\sigma$ for the canonical derived tensor symmetry. For $B\in\mathrm{CTF}_Y$ and $M\in\mathrm{BC}_X$, define the forward left-coefficient projection to be $\sigma;\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,B};F_e(\sigma)$ from $B\otimes^LF_eM$ to $F_e(S_eB\otimes^LM)$, using the specified projection of [def-exchange-projection]; let $\pi^e_{B,M}$ be its inverse on this domain. Whenever $W_e\in\mathrm{CTF}_X$, define
$$\theta_{e,B}=\mathrm{hom}_e\bigl(\pi^e_{B,W_e};(1_B\otimes\varepsilon_{e,\Lambda_Y});\rho_B\bigr):S_eB\otimes^LW_e\longrightarrow G_eB,$$
where $\rho_B:B\otimes^L\Lambda_Y\simeq B$ is the right unitor and semicolons denote composition in the displayed order. This is precisely the specified canonical map of [def-pur-co-smoothness], clause (2), in left-coefficient coordinates; no cohomological smoothness assumption is used to define it.

For composable edges $e:X\to Y$, $d:Y\to Z$ and an independently retained bounded compactification of $h=gf$, let $\mathrm{compositeEdge}(e,d)$ retain that compactification and bound. Define $\alpha:F_dF_eM\simeq F_hM$ on bounded-below etale-origin inputs by the canonical changes to the standing compactifications, the canonical etale-origin compact-support compositor [thm-sf-comp-composition], and the change to the retained compactification of $h$, as in [def-pur-chosen-compactification-compositors]. The changes are conjugated by the retained origin isomorphism. Define
$$c_B=\mathrm{hom}_e\bigl(\mathrm{hom}_d(\alpha_{G_hB};\varepsilon_{h,B})\bigr):G_hB\longrightarrow G_eG_dB.$$
This is exactly the map of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition] in the three retained compactification coordinates. Also define its reverse representing map, without asserting an inverse equation as part of this definition, by
$$\bar c_B=\mathrm{hom}_h\bigl(\alpha_{G_eG_dB}^{-1};F_d(\varepsilon_{e,G_dB});\varepsilon_{d,B}\bigr):G_eG_dB\longrightarrow G_hB.$$
All displayed functors and maps are the canonical constructions just specified, rather than arbitrary maps or choices of isomorphisms.
